working_tree: uncommitted changes on the branch above; the script and gated test are the committed evidence

environment.qdrant_client: qdrant-client 1.18.0 (client major matches; minor is 6 ahead of the server — outside Qdrant's documented support window, see compatibility_risk)
environment.redis: redis:7-alpine, 127.0.0.1:6379 db 15 (disposable), for the cache-key isolation check

compatibility_risk.policy: Qdrant documents that major and minor versions of the client and server are expected to match, and that backward compatibility is tested across one minor version only.
compatibility_risk.observed_behaviour: All 20 functional checks pass against the 1.12.0 server with the 1.18.0 client.
compatibility_risk.risk: Empirical success is not a support guarantee. An API or wire change in client 1.13-1.18 is not covered by Qdrant's stated compatibility window for a 1.12.0 server.
compatibility_risk.why_not_changed: Aligning the client would be a dependency change beyond the scope of this evidence fix; the gap is recorded here and in docs/validation/qdrant-local-real-validation.md instead of being silently absorbed.

embedding.note: deterministic vectors validate the storage engine, filters and fusion contract only; BGE/CLIP model quality is not measured

observations.epoch_scoping: every dense hit carries the active doc_version_epoch; the epoch-B filter returns only epoch-B points
observations.rbac_before_fusion: is_document_authorized yields different visible sets for two identities; role A cannot see role-B documents
observations.collection_separation: dense hits come from the text collection; the image hit comes from the image collection
observations.text_image_fusion: the real rrf_fusion merges text and image sources into one ranked list
observations.epoch_point_id_isolation: epoch-A and epoch-B point ids are disjoint and coexist
observations.dependency_degradation: the dense path logs the failure and returns empty when Qdrant is unreachable
observations.cache_key_isolation: the cache key changes with both the knowledge epoch and the permission fingerprint; a real Redis round-trip does not leak across identities

counts_source.method: derived by check_counts() from the executed check records, not written by hand
counts_source.guard: tests/validation/test_qdrant_validation_evidence.py fails if these counts disagree with checks.json

limitations: Single host, single node. No Qdrant cluster, replica, HA, TLS or throughput measurement.
Deterministic vectors, so no BGE/CLIP/PaddleOCR model-quality claim.
Not a production-cluster result; production HA/SLO remain PENDING.
The capture reflects the working tree at commit 6d2576e plus the uncommitted changes on the branch; a re-run reproduces the same checks.
